red.focus: Build a legal explanation with a claim, rule, facts, and conclusion.
red.summary: An argument is more than saying that an outcome feels fair. Learn to state a focused legal question, identify a valid rule, show how the facts satisfy or fail its conditions, and reach a careful conclusion.
checklist: I can state an issue without assuming its answer
I can connect one legally relevant fact to a rule
I can give a qualified conclusion rather than a promise

sections.title: An argument answers one question
sections.body_md: A customer claims that a merchant failed to deliver a paid-for item. The customer wants a refund. First ask which legal system and contract terms govern, whether payment and promised delivery are documented, and whether any legally recognized excuse applies. The question could be framed: Did the seller breach an enforceable delivery obligation, and what relief may follow? The wording matters because it tells the listener what must be decided. Anger alone cannot establish a breach, and a sympathetic client still needs legally relevant facts.

Anger alone cannot establish a breach, and a sympathetic client still needs legally relevant facts.

sections.title: Connect a rule to evidence
sections.body_md: Suppose the contract required shipment by September 1 and a tracking record indicates no shipment by September 10. The legal rule may require proof of a binding obligation, nonperformance, and a remedy under governing law. Put the contract beside the rule, and explain what the tracking record does and does not show. The seller might offer a valid contractual extension or evidence of delivery. A useful argument should acknowledge that possibility rather than pretending contrary information does not exist. The evidence makes the explanation checkable.

sections.title: Conclude without overpromising
sections.body_md: The conclusion can say that the buyer appears to have a viable nonperformance claim if the shipment date was binding and no valid excuse exists. Next steps include checking contractual remedies and local filing requirements. This is better than saying the customer will certainly win or that the seller should be punished. Clear legal writing uses simple connecting words—because, however, therefore—to show why facts matter. Its purpose is to help a person understand a decision and options, not merely impress them with complicated vocabulary.

yellow.focus: Write a structured IRAC or CREAC analysis with a fair counterargument.
yellow.summary: Issue–Rule–Application–Conclusion and Conclusion–Rule–Explanation–Application–Conclusion are frameworks for clear legal reasoning. Use them to make each element testable, incorporate authority accurately, and answer the strongest opposing claim.
checklist: I can organize one element of a claim using IRAC or CREAC
I can use an authoritative source instead of a vague slogan
I can write and answer a plausible counterargument

sections.title: Structure follows the question
sections.body_md: A pedestrian is injured when a shop's delivery cart rolls onto a walkway. The issue might be whether the shop breached a duty of reasonable care. State the jurisdiction's governing negligence rule; then identify the duty's relevant conditions and cases. Describe what the shop knew about a defective brake and what precautions were feasible, separating established facts from testimony still in dispute. Conclude on that element, not the entire lawsuit. The IRAC framework is a memory aid; it cannot replace verifying the rule and evidence.
sections.audio_script: A pedestrian is injured when a shop's delivery cart rolls onto a walkway. The issue might be whether the shop breached a duty of reasonable care. State the jurisdiction's governing negligence rule; then identify the duty's relevant conditions and cases. Describe what the shop knew about a defective brake and what precautions were feasible, separating established facts from testimony still in dispute. Conclude on that element, not the entire lawsuit. The IRAC framework is a memory aid; it cannot replace verifying the rule and evidence.

sections.title: Authority needs explanation, not decoration
sections.body_md: A brief should not list three cases without saying why each matters. Explain a holding's material facts, legal principle, and relationship to the delivery cart. An earlier case involving a similar defect may support foreseeability; another involving an unforeseeable external force may be distinguishable. Check subsequent treatment before calling any case controlling. CREAC places the tentative conclusion up front, then gives the rule and its explanation before application and final conclusion. Either organization should make the chain of reasoning accessible to an unfamiliar reader.
sections.audio_script: A brief should not list three cases without saying why each matters. Explain a holding's material facts, legal principle, and relationship to the delivery cart. An earlier case involving a similar defect may support foreseeability; another involving an unforeseeable external force may be distinguishable. Check subsequent treatment before calling any case controlling. CREAC places the tentative conclusion up front, then gives the rule and its explanation before application and final conclusion. Either organization should make the chain of reasoning accessible to an unfamiliar reader.

sections.title: Answer the best opposing argument
sections.body_md: The shop may assert that a stranger moved the cart after staff had secured it. If evidence supports that account, it can affect breach or causation. State the strongest version of the defense and explain what testimony or record would distinguish it from the pedestrian's theory. A weak rebuttal that calls the shop dishonest without evidence may damage credibility. The conclusion should identify the evidentiary hinge and recommended next inquiry. Good advocacy is not a refusal to acknowledge a real risk; it is a precise explanation of why one legal result is better supported.

Good advocacy is not a refusal to acknowledge a real risk; it is a precise explanation of why one legal result is better supported.

orange.focus: Construct appellate arguments from text, precedent, standard of review and remedy.
orange.summary: An appellate position must identify what was preserved, which legal question the reviewing court can decide, and the standard governing each issue. Build a persuasive brief without confusing factual dispute with legal error.
checklist: I can separate an appealable legal error from disputed fact
I can connect the standard of review to the argument's structure
I can state an authorized remedy proportionate to the alleged error

sections.title: Know what the reviewing tribunal can do
sections.body_md: A trial court excludes a witness and enters judgment. The dissatisfied party wants the appeal court to rehear everything, but appellate jurisdiction and standards of review may limit that ambition. Begin with the precise decision, the authority for review, whether the point was preserved, and any requirement to show prejudice. A question about interpreting a statute may receive different review from a factual finding or evidentiary ruling. A master's-level argument cannot simply declare the trial judge wrong without naming the legal route by which correction is possible.
sections.audio_script: A trial court excludes a witness and enters judgment. The dissatisfied party wants the appeal court to rehear everything, but appellate jurisdiction and standards of review may limit that ambition. Begin with the precise decision, the authority for review, whether the point was preserved, and any requirement to show prejudice. A question about interpreting a statute may receive different review from a factual finding or evidentiary ruling. A master's-level argument cannot simply declare the trial judge wrong without naming the legal route by which correction is possible.

sections.title: Organize each proposition around authority
sections.body_md: State the applicable standard of review before relying on cases that govern a different posture. Then give the challenged ruling, controlling legal test, record citations, error alleged, and why it mattered to the outcome. A precedent concerning clear error may not support a demand for unrestricted reconsideration of witness credibility. Use a carefully explained analogy and address adverse binding cases. A well-structured appellate argument narrows the dispute to something the tribunal can legitimately decide. It should not smuggle in facts outside the record as though they were established below.

Then give the challenged ruling, controlling legal test, record citations, error alleged, and why it mattered to the outcome. A well-structured appellate argument narrows the dispute to something the tribunal can legitimately decide. It should not smuggle in facts outside the record as though they were established below.

sections.title: Ask for relief the court may grant
sections.body_md: Even an established mistake may not justify a new trial if governing harmless-error principles apply. Explain how the error affected substantial rights where that is required. The requested remedy might be reversal, remand, reconsideration, or a narrower direction, depending on law and posture. Distinguish a victory on a legal proposition from practical relief for the client. Test the best opposing case: perhaps the excluded witness was cumulative or the ruling fell within authorized discretion. A strong brief gives the court a lawful path to the result it requests.

black.focus: Design an ethically legitimate theory of persuasive adjudicative reasons.
black.summary: Persuasive legal arguments must work within institutional authority while acknowledging uncertainty, values and the people affected by a decision. Synthesize doctrinal rigor, practical consequences, interpretive theory and professional candor.
checklist: I can identify hidden normative assumptions in an otherwise technical argument
I can balance institutional competence with legal principle and effects
I can design a reasoned position that addresses adverse authority and affected persons

sections.title: Reasoning needs premises that can be challenged
sections.body_md: A constitutional challenge may rely on a textual command, judicial precedent, and a policy prediction about how restrictions affect minorities. Those are different types of premises. A doctoral argument makes their status explicit: what source binds, what principle is contested, what empirical claim requires support, and what result the institution may lawfully deliver. Do not invoke dignity or liberty as decorative words without explaining their legal relationship to the dispute. The opposing party should be able to identify the real point of disagreement instead of guessing at the advocate's assumptions.

Do not invoke dignity or liberty as decorative words without explaining their legal relationship to the dispute. The opposing party should be able to identify the real point of disagreement instead of guessing at the advocate's assumptions.

sections.title: Candor is part of persuasive strength
sections.body_md: In jurisdictions following rules akin to the American Bar Association's Model Rule 3.3, an advocate owes duties not to make knowingly false statements and, in specified circumstances, to disclose directly adverse controlling authority the opponent has not identified. Local professional rules govern; the model provision is not a universal code. Acknowledging a damaging case can help the court trust the lawyer's distinction or request for principled reconsideration. Hiding authority may temporarily simplify a narrative but undermines adjudication and exposes the client to legal and professional risk.

Hiding authority may temporarily simplify a narrative but undermines adjudication and exposes the client to legal and professional risk.

sections.title: Build a remedy-centered constitutional argument
sections.body_md: Suppose a benefits system systematically denies applicants with limited language access. A robust argument identifies statutory procedures, applicable equality rights, institutional competence, evidence of impact, and the strongest legitimate administrative justification. It then proposes relief proportionate to the proven wrong, with attention to the applicants who urgently need support. Compare competing interpretations fairly and explain why one is superior under governing law. The best position does not just win a rhetorical contest; it gives the tribunal a defensible decision, a workable remedy, and public reasons for the people who must live with it.
